title: The Lunch Hour on the Riachuelo: Barracas to San Luca and Back
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Barracas, birth by the Riachuelo
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Barracas takes the tide of the Riachuelo before the embankments tame it: tanneries, wool sheds, cart tracks, Italian spoken the length of the street beside Spanish. Into that quarter, on the twentieth of August, a son is born to an immigrant family out of Italy. Buenos Aires still counts its age in decades. The boy grows up within walking distance of the water he will spend fifty years painting, though nothing here marks him for it yet. The river is the ground he walks on, and wet hides are what the air smells of.
suggested_refs: The Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes necrology of Collivadino, and Parker, Argentinos de hoy (1920), both cited at second hand

stops.name: Società Nazionale Italiana, the first drawing lessons
stops.date_confidence: no source gives a year; c. 1885-1889 is inferred backwards from the 1889 departure, and the society's premises are unlocated, so the pin is an approximation of the centre
stops.campa: The Italian community of Buenos Aires keeps a classroom, and the sons of immigrants are taught in it the old academic discipline: proportion, cast shadow, the human figure built up stroke by stroke. A maestro named Luzzi corrects him. He is not yet twenty and has never seen a European gallery, only reproductions and the plaster casts a young republic can afford to import. The lessons are modest, and no source names one drawing he made in that room. Within four years he is on a ship for Italy, going to fetch the rest of it.
suggested_refs: Records of the Società Nazionale Italiana of Buenos Aires, which would fix the years and the premises, unconsulted

stops.name: Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes, the drawing rooms
stops.date_confidence: attendance attested without any dates; Ángel della Valle's eighteen-year teaching post at the same institution overlaps these years, but no source states that he taught Collivadino
stops.campa: He goes on to the Estímulo, founded eleven years before by Eduardo Sívori, Eduardo Schiaffino and a handful of others to give the city the art teaching the state does not provide. Ángel della Valle has been correcting drawing in these rooms since the early eighties, three sessions a week, charcoal and plaster casts and the figure broken into planes. Argentina has no national academy. It has this room. The pupil passing through it now will be running the country's academy in twenty years, administering by decree what he learned in a borrowed classroom.
suggested_refs: Enrolment books of the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes for the 1880s, which would settle whether della Valle taught him

stops.name: Genoa, the crossing run in reverse
stops.date_confidence: the year of departure is attested; the port is undocumented and Genoa is reconstruction from the shipping route of the period
stops.campa: He crosses in 1889, one more young man on the Italy to River Plate route, running it the wrong way. No manifest reached names his ship or his port; Genoa is where the traffic of these years puts in, and it stands here on that ground alone. What is certain is the direction. His people came west out of Italy into a tanning quarter on a South American river; he sails east to claim from the old country an education the new one cannot yet give. He will not see Buenos Aires again for seven years.
suggested_refs: Passenger manifests of the Genoa lines for 1889, unconsulted; the port remains open
sources: No source for the port; reconstruction stated as such

stops.name: Rome, two undocumented years
stops.date_confidence: the year of arrival is attested; the month is unknown and defaulted, and the two years before admission are blank in every source
stops.campa: Rome receives him at twenty. Two years pass before the academy admits him, and no source reached says how he spends them: drawing schools, a copyist's wage, the free schools of the nude, the ordinary apprenticeship of a foreigner waiting on an examination. The city is the capital of a kingdom nineteen years old, digging its ministries out of papal ground and hiring painters by the yard to decorate them. He arrives into a building boom that needs hands, and into an academic tradition that will not be hurried by it.
suggested_refs: Roman residence and school registers for 1889-1891, which would fill two blank years, unconsulted

stops.name: Accademia di San Luca, the examination passed
stops.date_confidence: the year of admission is attested by both language versions; no month or day is given
stops.campa: In 1891 the Accademia di San Luca admits him, the old company of painters and architects that has examined Roman draughtsmen since the sixteenth century. Admission is not automatic for a foreigner from a republic most of the professors could not place on a map. He enters halls hung with three centuries of Roman drawing and begins the course, which puts line ahead of colour and the figure ahead of everything else. Barracas recedes. What is built here is the method he will later impose on a national school.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the Accademia di San Luca, 1891

stops.name: Rome, under the hand of Cesare Mariani
stops.date_confidence: the pupillage is attested and undated; it runs 1891-1896, not the 1891-1898 some summaries give, since the return to Buenos Aires is fixed at 1896
stops.campa: Cesare Mariani takes him in hand: fresco painter, accademico di San Luca since 1863, president of the academy until the year before Collivadino reached Rome, a teacher who lets no pupil skip a stage. Five years the bond holds. Fresco is arithmetic as much as paint, lime and sand and the day's patch of wet plaster that must be finished before it sets, and it teaches a man to plan in the morning a wall he cannot revise in the evening. Every student he later corrects in Buenos Aires inherits that rigour with the name stripped off it.
suggested_refs: it.wikipedia, 'Cesare Mariani (pittore)': accademico di San Luca 1863, president 1888-1890, frescoes at San Paolo fuori le mura and the Palazzo delle Finanze

stops.name: Palazzo di Giustizia, scaffolding on the Tiber
stops.date_confidence: contested throughout: no source places Mariani at this building, its fresco cycle is Cesare Maccari's and postdates Collivadino's Roman years, and the 'Constitutional Court of Italy' the English source names did not exist until 1948; the date is a placeholder inside the student years
stops.campa: On the right bank a hall of justice is going up, a marble mountain that will take twenty-two years and swallow a small army of decorators. His biography puts him on the scaffolding of it as a student, learning mural painting where murals are actually made rather than where they are taught. The record fights itself here. The building's own fresco cycle belongs to another painter of a nearly identical name and was begun after he sailed home. What the accounts share is only the trade: wet plaster on a scaffold, against a wall too large for one man.
suggested_refs: it.wikipedia, 'Palazzo di Giustizia (Roma)': built 1889-1911, Aula Magna frescoes by Cesare Maccari, abandoned 1909, completed by Paride Pascucci to 1918

stops.name: Paris, the countries without cities
stops.date_confidence: the European travels are attested only as a list of countries, with no dates, cities or order; Paris is a placeholder for an undocumented itinerary
stops.campa: France, Germany, Holland, Belgium, England: his biography lists the countries and gives no city, no year, no order. Paris stands here for that itinerary, being where an academic student of the 1890s goes to see what is being done against the academy. The Salons are enormous, and the Impressionists are twenty years old and no longer a scandal. A fresco painter's apprentice looks at easel pictures of ordinary people in ordinary light. Nine years later he paints workmen eating lunch on the ground and Venice gives it a gold medal.
suggested_refs: Any documentation of the European circuit named in biografiasyvidas: no city, date or route is recorded anywhere reached
sources: No source for Paris specifically; placeholder stated as such

stops.name: London, the end of the northern circuit
stops.date_confidence: England is named among the countries visited and nothing else is; the year and the city placement are both placeholders
stops.campa: England is on the list too, and nothing survives of what he saw there, whom he met, or how long he stayed. The whole northern circuit is one sentence in a biographical dictionary and no sentence anywhere else: France, Germany, Holland, Belgium, England, in that order or another. What can be said is its shape: a young Argentine carrying a Roman method walks through galleries in four languages in the last years before he goes home for good. What he made of them is not on any page reached, and his own letters from those months sit unread in a volume printed a century later.
suggested_refs: Malosetti Costa, Cuadros de viaje (FCE, 2008), said to print Collivadino's own European letters; not obtained, and the likeliest source to fix this circuit
sources: biografiasyvidas.com, 'Pío Collivadino' (England named among five countries)

segments.name: The Return and the Mouth of the River

stops.name: Port of Buenos Aires, landing formed
stops.date_confidence: 1896 attested by both language versions; the 'seven-year course at the academy' they also give is incompatible with an 1891 admission and is counted here from the 1889 sailing instead
stops.campa: He lands in 1896 after seven years away, carrying a San Luca training and five years of fresco under Mariani. The city has thickened while he was gone, new money and new immigrants and a port being dug out of the mud at Madero. He is twenty-six and has no commissions. The seven years his biographers credit to the academy are counted from this quay back to the sailing, not from the year San Luca took him in; the arithmetic in his own life story does not close, and it has been copied unclosed ever since.
suggested_refs: Argentine arrival registers for 1896, which would give the vessel and the date, unconsulted

stops.name: La Boca, the lithograph years
stops.date_confidence: the lithograph period is attested without dates or titles; La Boca as his working ground in these years is reconstruction from his recurring subjects
stops.campa: He works as a lithographer, romantic in manner, and the work is praised. Not one plate is named in any source reached. What is known is the subject he begins to circle: the mouth of the Riachuelo, tin-sided houses, cargo cranes, barges laid over on the mud at low water, laundry strung between balconies by Genoese dockers who came the way his parents came. Rome had taught him how to build a picture. Here he settles what to build one out of, and the decision holds for the rest of his working life.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires print-shop catalogues of the later 1890s; not one Collivadino lithograph is titled in any source reached

stops.name: Buenos Aires, La hora del almuerzo painted
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested; the research pool's alternate title 'La hora del reposo' is supported by no source consulted and is dropped
stops.campa: He finishes La hora del almuerzo: labourers seated on the ground in the hard daylight of the port, eating from tin plates in the middle of a working day. There is no allegory in it, no history, no myth, no woman draped as a virtue. It is a lunch break, painted at the size and with the seriousness a European jury reserves for a battle or a saint. Then he sends it to Venice. Whatever is modest about the subject, the gesture is not: he is proposing that a shift break on the Riachuelo will carry a full-dress academic picture.
suggested_refs: La hora del almuerzo, oil, 1903, Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires
sources: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes collection records

stops.name: Venice, the gold medal for a lunch break
stops.date_confidence: attested by both language versions
stops.campa: The international exhibition at Venice gives its gold medal to the lunch hour of the Buenos Aires docks. A jury used to allegory and portraiture hands its highest award to men eating on the ground beside a river most of them have never heard of. He is thirty-four and seven years back from Europe. The Argentine art world of the day accepts one kind of proof, a European verdict, and he has now been handed it for a picture of dockhands at their food. The painting will end in the national collection.
suggested_refs: Prize lists of the Venice international exhibition of 1903

stops.name: St Louis, gold and silver at the World's Fair
stops.date_confidence: the medals and the year are attested; the works exhibited are not named in any source reached
stops.campa: The Louisiana Purchase Exposition hands him gold and silver in the same year, a doubled award one season after Venice. Argentina has come to Forest Park to argue that it is a modern productive nation, and canvases of docks and daily labour make that case better than the wheat statistics in the pavilion behind them. Which works hung there is recorded nowhere reached. What is recorded is the pair of medals, collected in Missouri by a painter from Barracas for pictures of a river six thousand miles to the south.
suggested_refs: Official award lists of the Louisiana Purchase Exposition, 1904, Argentine section

stops.name: Accademia di Brera, honorary academician
stops.date_confidence: the membership is attested and the year is not: es.wikipedia attaches 1905 to the Order of the Crown alone, biografiasyvidas gives no year at all, and this pin sits near the middle of a c. 1898-1908 range, placed before the 1905 crown so as not to borrow its date
stops.campa: Brera makes him an honorary academician. The year is fixed by no source: the Spanish account attaches 1905 to the Italian crown and leaves the Milanese honour dateless, the English account lets the date slide onto both, the Spanish dictionary gives none. What is not in doubt is the title. The other pole of Italian painting, the one that is not Rome, adds its name to his, and a painter from Barracas is tied to Italy by two institutions his parents could never have walked into.
suggested_refs: Membership rolls of the Accademia di Brera, Milan, which would date the honour

stops.name: Rome, the Order of the Crown of Italy
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested; the venue is reconstruction from ordinary practice, and no source names a place, a ceremony or a grade
stops.campa: Italy decorates him with the Order of the Crown, the honour the kingdom keeps for those who carry its prestige abroad. Neither the grade nor the ceremony is described anywhere reached; investitures of the sort are held at the royal court in Rome, and this placement rests on that custom and nothing else. The symmetry is the substance of it. A family left Italy for a tanning quarter on a South American river, and thirty-six years later the kingdom they left pins a cross on the son who was born there.
suggested_refs: Registers of the Ordine della Corona d'Italia for 1905, which would give the grade and the date, unconsulted

stops.name: Venice, the second showing
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia attests three Venice exhibitions from 1903 to 1907, so the Biennale years are 1903, 1905 and 1907; the works shown in the later two are unnamed
stops.campa: He shows at Venice again. The gold medal of two years before has fixed his name with the international juries, and this appearance consolidates rather than launches. What hung in the Argentine rooms in 1905 is not recorded in anything reached. Honours gather around the exhibitions rather than out of them: the Italian crown in this same year, the Milanese academy somewhere near it. It is his second crossing to the lagoon in three years, and a third will follow in 1907.
suggested_refs: Catalogues of the Venice Biennale of 1905, Argentine entries
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Pío Collivadino' ('tres exposiciones internacionales en Venecia, de 1903 a 1907')

stops.name: Venice, the third and last
stops.date_confidence: the third exhibition falls inside the attested 1903-1907 span; the year is the Biennale year and the works are unnamed
stops.campa: A third and last appearance at Venice closes the cycle begun in 1903. He has shown at the lagoon more often by now than almost any Argentine painter of his generation, and the gravel of the Giardini is as familiar to him as the wharf at the Vuelta de Rocha. After this he does not go back. A directorship at home is one year away and will hold him for twenty-seven, and the exhibiting career gives way to staff registers and the correction of other people's drawing.
suggested_refs: Catalogues of the Venice Biennale of 1907, Argentine entries

stops.name: Buenos Aires, joining Grupo Nexus
stops.date_confidence: the founding year 1907 is attested; the rosters disagree, English sources adding Martín Malharro whom no Spanish source lists and whose own article never mentions the group
stops.campa: He joins Grupo Nexus, the alliance the painter Fernando Fader and the sculptor Rogelio Yrurtia are leading against pure academic imitation of Europe, with Carlos Ripamonte, Cesáreo Bernaldo de Quirós, Ceferino Carnacini, Alberto María Rossi and Arturo Dresco. There is no manifesto, only a conviction: the port, the pampa and the tenement will carry the same seriousness as a mythology. Fader leads and Collivadino joins, though half the summaries written since have promoted him to founder.
suggested_refs: Rosters of Grupo Nexus as carried in the es.wikipedia articles on Carnacini, Ripamonte, Rossi and Dresco
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Pío Collivadino' ('se incorporó al Grupo Nexus')

stops.name: Av. Las Heras 1749, director of the national academy
stops.date_confidence: the directorship and the year are attested; that his academy sat in the Av. Las Heras 1749 building is institutional continuity, documented for the school and not for him personally
stops.campa: At thirty-nine he is made director of the Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, the school the state nationalised in 1905 out of the drawing workshops the Sociedad Estímulo had been running since 1878. The man who learned charcoal in those borrowed rooms as a boy now signs for them. He holds the post twenty-seven years, and in that time the method he brought back from Mariani becomes the state's own way of teaching art: plaster before life, the wall planned before it can be painted. What a few private citizens started in 1878 is now a state instrument, and it teaches what he was taught in Rome.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes Prilidiano Pueyrredón': 1878 workshops, 1905 nationalisation, Av. Las Heras 1749

stops.name: Plaza San Martín, the Centenary Exhibition
stops.date_confidence: his prominence at the Centenary exhibition is attested; the venue is corrected from Palermo to the Pabellón Argentino at Plaza San Martín, where es.wikipedia places the Bellas Artes section
stops.campa: For the centenary of the May Revolution the country stages an international exhibition and puts the Bellas Artes section in the Pabellón Argentino on calle Arenales, beside the Plaza San Martín; the livestock and the machinery go out to Palermo. Collivadino is among the painters displayed, two years into his directorship. The state that had no art school at all a generation ago is now exhibiting its painters to the world as evidence of arrival. He is no longer a promising exhibitor. He is the face the country chooses to show.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Exposición Internacional del Centenario': Bellas Artes in the Pabellón Argentino, calle Arenales at Plaza San Martín

stops.name: La Boca, the pupil Quinquela Martín
stops.date_confidence: the teacher and pupil relation is attested without dates; Quinquela Martín's formative study falls c. 1907-1912, so the summaries placing this in the 1920s and 1930s are too late, and the classroom is not documented
stops.campa: Among the pupils who pass through his teaching is Benito Quinquela Martín, born in 1890, a foundling of La Boca who will become the most popular painter Argentina produces and who paints the same water his teacher paints. The two share a subject and share nothing else in the handling of it: the master's restrained tonal realism, the pupil's thick slabs of colour laid on with a knife. Collivadino gives him the drawing discipline of San Luca, and he spends a career using it on surfaces the academy had no use for.
suggested_refs: Enrolment records of the Academia de la Sociedad Unión de La Boca and the national academy, c. 1907-1912

stops.name: Las Heras 1749, the chair of sculpture filled
stops.date_confidence: both posts are attested from separate sources and neither biography mentions the other man; the 1915 start of Troiani's chair is itself inferred from his arrival, and no document reached puts the two in a room together
stops.campa: Down the corridor from the director's office a Friulian sculptor takes the chair of sculpture: Troiano Troiani, five years off the boat from Buja by way of Venice and Rome, who will teach modelling on Las Heras for decades and cast caryatids for the city legislature. Two men formed in Italian academies now hold the figure teaching of an Argentine one between them, one at the drawing stands and one at the clay. Neither man's biography mentions the other. They are in the same building for twenty years.
suggested_refs: Staff registers of the Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, which would document the working relation; unconsulted, and no student of either man is named in common

stops.name: Vuelta de Rocha, the bend painted again and again
stops.date_confidence: the industrial river subjects are attested through the paintings themselves; this vantage and these years are reconstruction, no sketching site or studio being documented
stops.campa: Where the Riachuelo bends hard before it reaches the Plata he sets up again and again through these years. Barges list against the current, cranes swing cargo over water thickened with tannery runoff, the smell comes up off the mud at low tide the way it did when he was a boy half a mile upstream. The bend is not scenery. It is the fixed subject of his mature work, painted now with a professional's method instead of a child's familiarity, and he keeps coming back to it for thirty years.
suggested_refs: Collivadino's sketchbooks of the Riachuelo, which would fix his vantages; whereabouts unestablished in any source reached
sources: Reconstruction from the geography of the known works, stated as such

stops.name: Dock Sud, the power plants of Usinas
stops.date_confidence: the painting and its year are attested; the specific plant and its location are reconstruction from the geography his other works favour
stops.campa: He paints Usinas: smokestacks, turbine halls, the riverside power plants of an electrifying city. No source names the plant he worked from, and the industrial belt running south from the Riachuelo toward Dock Sud is the likeliest ground on the evidence of his other pictures. Machinery is given the frontal seriousness of a portrait, without smoke-and-progress rhetoric and without disgust, exactly as the men eating on the ground were given it eleven years before.
suggested_refs: Usinas, oil, 1914; the plant depicted is unidentified in every source reached

stops.name: La Boca, El Riachuelo finished
stops.date_confidence: the painting, its year and its place in the MNBA permanent collection are attested; the riverside vantage is reconstruction
stops.campa: El Riachuelo, painted in 1916, is the mature return to the water. It will hang in the national collection beside La hora del almuerzo, the two canvases bracketing thirteen years and the whole industrial middle of a life. Where he stood to paint it is not recorded, and a picture of this kind compresses several vantages into one river in any case. He is forty-seven, running the academy by day, decorated by a kingdom, and still going down to the same bend of the same creek with a board under his arm.
suggested_refs: El Riachuelo, oil, 1916, Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires
sources: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes collection records

stops.name: Teatro Colón, scenery and the board
stops.date_confidence: both roles are attested and every source leaves them undated; the 1920s placement is a placeholder inside the decades after 1908
stops.campa: He directs stage design at the Teatro Colón and later sits as president of its board. No source reached gives a year for either post; the decades after the academy directorship began are all that can be said. Scenography is the opposite discipline to the one he practises on the river: built to be read from forty metres, under electric light, and to dissolve into illusion the moment the curtain goes up. The realist of the docks spends his evenings manufacturing unreality at a scale no easel allows.
suggested_refs: Minutes and production records of the Teatro Colón, which would date both the scenography post and the presidency; unconsulted

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the theatre called La Higuerita
stops.date_confidence: the name and the existence are attested by es.wikipedia and by nothing else; the date and the location are wholly undocumented, and both the year and this pin are placeholders
stops.campa: He builds a theatre of his own and calls it La Higuerita, the little fig tree. That is the whole of the record: a name, and the fact that it existed. No address, no year, no company, no repertoire, no photograph reached. An old painter with a national academy on his shoulders and the Colón's stage machinery in his head makes himself a small room where plays can be put on to please nobody but himself, and then a century of paperwork loses it completely.
suggested_refs: Municipal theatre licences and the Buenos Aires press of the 1920s and 1930s, which would locate La Higuerita; unconsulted

stops.name: Tandil, granite instead of cranes
stops.date_confidence: the painting is attested by title; the trips that produced it are undated and both the year and the sierra location are reconstruction
stops.campa: He goes out to Tandil, into the granite sierras of the province, and paints Paisaje de Tandil. It is a departure: no cranes, no barges, no smoke, only weathered rock and the pampa horizon behind it. No source dates the trips; they belong somewhere in his mature period, and the year on this stop is a placeholder. The sierra gives him what the Riachuelo cannot, distance and rock that was standing there long before any port his family crossed an ocean to reach.
suggested_refs: Paisaje de Tandil; no source dates the journeys to the sierras or names a host or a stay
sources: Reconstruction for the trips, stated as such

stops.name: Av. Las Heras 1749, retirement from teaching
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested by all three principal sources; no month or day is given
stops.campa: At sixty-six he retires from teaching. Twenty-seven years of classrooms end, in which he has put the Roman method into the hands of Lino Enea Spilimbergo, Héctor Basaldúa, Quinquela Martín and a generation whose names now fill the Argentine museums, and set up specialised decoration workshops besides. The institutional life does not end with the teaching; two more directorships lie ahead of him. What closes is the room, and the daily labour of standing in front of it correcting other people's drawing.
suggested_refs: The pupil lists in biografiasyvidas: Spilimbergo, Basaldúa and Quinquela Martín attested; Raquel Forner appears in weaker summaries only

stops.name: Escuela Prilidiano Pueyrredón, the last directorship
stops.date_confidence: the 1939 appointment and the 1944 end are attested; the school takes the Pueyrredón name only by decree in 1940, so the post predates the name it is always given
stops.campa: At seventy he is put in as interim director of the Manuel Belgrano preparatory school and helps organise the Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes that will take the name of Prilidiano Pueyrredón by decree the following year. He directs it until 1944. He is seventy-four when the term ends. The men who built a national art school out of a private drawing circle are nearly all dead by now, and he is still signing for it, thirty-six years after he first took charge.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes Prilidiano Pueyrredón': Decree 72154 of 1940 for the renaming

stops.name: Costanera Sur, the museum of plaster casts
stops.date_confidence: flatly contested: the Collivadino articles give 1941 and a founding role, while the museum's own article gives inauguration in 1928, public opening in 1932, de la Cárcova's name from the outset, and never mentions him; this stop follows the date his biographers assert and records that the institution denies it
stops.campa: His biographies credit him with helping found the Museum of Casts and Comparative Sculpture on the Costanera Sur, the plaster archive that gives students in a city with no antiquities a Laocoon to draw from. The museum's own record does not know him. It was inaugurated in 1928, opened to the public in 1932, and carried Ernesto de la Cárcova's name from the start. Thirteen years and one whole institution stand between the two accounts, and neither of them gives way.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Museo de la Cárcova', Av. España 1701: inaugurated 1928, opened 1932 under Ángel Guido, no mention of Collivadino
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Museo de la Cárcova' (counter-evidence and coordinates)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, removed by the military government
stops.date_confidence: both language versions give 1944 under General Pedro Pablo Ramírez, who was deposed on 24 February 1944, so a dismissal by his government falls in the first eight weeks of the year; Geno Díaz's memoir instead dates the expulsion to the coup of 4 June 1943, and the two accounts are not reconciled here
stops.campa: The military government removes him. He is seventy-four and has held one post or another in the national art schools since 1908, and the regime thrown up by the coup wants the European inheritance out of them. The dismissal ends his working life, thirty-six years after he first signed for the academy, and he outlives it by a year and a half. His own pupils tell it more bluntly than the encyclopaedias do, as an old master thrown out of the school he had given his life to and replaced by an incompetent.
stops.quote: El 4 de junio [de 1943], estalló la revolución, y expulsó al director de la escuela, don Pío Collivadino, un hombre de grandes conocimientos técnicos, un reconocido artista que había dedicado su vida a la Escuela. [...] Fue cruelmente reemplazado por uno de esos perversos incompetentes, y el ilustre maestro anciano murió de tristeza.
stops.quote_source: Geno Díaz, Genocidio II (Buenos Aires: Emecé Editores, 1985), p. 20, quoted as a block quotation in es.wikipedia, 'Pío Collivadino', note 7; verified at the Wikipedia layer only, and Díaz is a memoirist, so 'murió de tristeza' is his framing and not a finding
suggested_refs: The 1944 dismissal file of the Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes Prilidiano Pueyrredón, which would settle the month and the signature; unconsulted
sources: Geno Díaz, Genocidio II (1985), p. 20, via es.wikipedia note 7

stops.name: Buenos Aires, death six days after the birthday
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both language versions
stops.campa: He dies in Buenos Aires on the twenty-sixth of August, six days after his seventy-sixth birthday and a year and a half after the dismissal. The city held everything except the European years: the birth in Barracas, the borrowed classroom, the lithographs, the medals brought home from Venice and Missouri, twenty-seven years at the head of the academy, the theatre with the fig-tree name. The river he painted runs past the funeral carrying the same barges, which are by then permanent in oil.
suggested_refs: The Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes necrology of Collivadino, cited by es.wikipedia and not consulted directly

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a grave nobody records
stops.date_confidence: the burial itself is undocumented: no cemetery, plot or pantheon is named in any biography, dictionary or encyclopaedia reached, and this date is the day after the death, not an attested interment
stops.campa: Where he was buried is not known. No cemetery, no plot, no pantheon is named in any biography or dictionary entry reached, and he is absent from the published lists of notable interments at Recoleta, where a man of his standing would ordinarily lie. Director of the national academy for twenty-seven years, decorated by the kingdom of Italy, medalled at Venice and at St Louis, and the ground that holds him is unrecorded. The city's cemetery registers for the winter of 1945 have not been searched.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires cemetery registers for August and September 1945; unconsulted, and the likeliest place to close this gap

stops.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, the two canvases
stops.date_confidence: the presence of both paintings in the permanent collection is attested and undated; this year stands for 'after his death' and is not an acquisition date
stops.campa: La hora del almuerzo and El Riachuelo hang in the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, thirteen years apart in the making and the whole industrial middle of a life between them. Visitors pass from the lunch break of 1903 to the river of 1916 without needing to know about San Luca, or Mariani's corrections, or three crossings to Venice, or twenty-seven years of staff meetings. The museum keeps the pictures. The itinerary that made them, Barracas to Rome and back, survives in footnotes.

stops.name: Banfield, the museum in his name
stops.date_confidence: opening in 1992, closure for restoration in 2010 and reopening in 2018 are attested; no month or day is given for any of the three
stops.campa: A museum bearing his name opens in Banfield, out on the southern line beyond the city limit, holding more than a hundred of his works. It closes in 2010 for restoration and stays shut eight years. When it reopens in 2018 the painter has been dead seventy-three years and the Riachuelo he painted is a byword for industrial poisoning, its cleanup a permanent item of national politics. The pictures in Banfield show the same water in the years when the smoke over it still counted as the future.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Malosetti Costa takes him up
stops.date_confidence: the imprint is dated 2006 by OpenLibrary and 2007 by the es.wikipedia references list; the contradiction is left standing
stops.campa: The art historian Laura Malosetti Costa publishes a monograph on him with El Ateneo, and the rehabilitation begins in earnest. In the same year an essayist puts the case in his title: a great forgotten painter. Sixty years after his death the man who ran Argentine art teaching for a generation has to be rescued from obscurity, and the scholar doing the rescuing reads his canvases as holding something other than the docks and cranes they depict. What she finds in them is time, not industry.
stops.quote: el perfume de otros tiempos, la nostalgia de lo apenas perdido

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the European letters printed
stops.date_confidence: the anthology, its editor and its year are attested from bookseller records; the volume itself was not obtained and its Collivadino contents are described at second hand
stops.campa: Malosetti Costa selects and prefaces an anthology of Argentine artists writing home from Europe and the United States between 1880 and 1910, ten of them, Collivadino among them. His own travel writing and correspondence from the European years are printed there. Everything the encyclopaedias cannot supply about Rome, the two blank years before San Luca, the countries listed without a single city, is the kind of thing that sits in a volume like this one, in his own hand.

stops.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires en construcción
stops.date_confidence: the MNBA edition of 2013 is confirmed by OpenLibrary and by the museum's own article; the research pool's 'Grupo Ilhsa 2014 trade edition' conflates it with the earlier El Ateneo imprint and with a separate 2014 Aguilar title
stops.campa: The national museum mounts Pío Collivadino. Buenos Aires en construcción, with a catalogue, and puts the argument in the subtitle: the painter of a city under construction. He watched Buenos Aires go from cart tracks and tanneries to a capital with power plants, a dredged port and an opera house, and he painted the transformation from inside it. A hundred and ten years after the lunch break on the docks, the museum that has kept the canvas hangs it as the evidence.
